unspecified_scores.reason: Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:139-151: the rootMargin is computed once when the observer is created (deps [firstRatio, state.numPages]), so after the window is resized or the phone sheet changes height, pages start drawing a little earlier or later than half a visible height away; at worst the user sees a brief white placeholder before a thumbnail appears, because cells still draw once they intersect the visible box.

Confirmed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:200 and 313-321: eviction checks only drawn.size, and cells in `entered` mount a <Page> without counting against the cap, so a fast fling through a long PDF's rail starts renders for every page passed; pdf.js then does wasted work and the rail may lag briefly before eviction brings drawn back to 120, but nothing visible is wrong and I3's cap on `drawn` still holds.

specification_compliance: No findings were submitted for verification.
I3's '120 drawn' cap is enforced in a layout effect (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:199-221), which evicts the cells farthest from the visible box's centre before paint; cells in 'drawing' are outside the cap.
I5: the only goToPage calls are cell and outline onClick handlers (PdfPagesPanel.tsx:284, 328); the follow effect only writes root.scrollTop (line 194).
I6: the follow effect centres the cell relative to visibleBox, which subtracts --inspector-sticky-top (lines 186-194, 405-417), and skips cells that are already wholly visible (line 188).

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: If firstRatio resolves while the Pages tab has already been switched away (hidden, zero-size scroller rect), the drawing margin computed at PdfPagesPanel.tsx:139-141 is 0 for the rest of the mount, so pages draw only when they actually enter the visible box.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Switching tabs within the moment between opening Pages and the first page's proportion loading leaves pages popping in on scroll instead of being pre-drawn half a screen ahead; nothing is lost.

regression_risks: Moving eviction from useEffect to useLayoutEffect makes it run getBoundingClientRect on up to ~120+ cells synchronously before paint whenever drawn exceeds the cap, which may cause a small layout-thrash cost during fast scrolls.
Evicted pages are also removed from `entered`; a page evicted while it is still near the visible box draws again only when its intersection changes.
test_coverage: PdfPagesPanel.test.tsx:532-538 checks that intersecting 125 pages leaves exactly 120 drawn; no test checks that the cap is applied before paint, or how many 'drawing' cells there are during a burst.
PdfPagesPanel.test.tsx:540-554 checks that an off-proportion page keeps its own box after it is evicted.
No unit test covers the rootMargin value or recomputing it on resize.
